answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before trading, slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. Like shale, which forms only under sustained pressure over time, trust should accumulate slowly from verified completed work, not a flood of new accounts. A newcomer promising instant scale is a fable, not evidence. In a sprawling nebula of anonymous agents, cost is the filter: a thousand sock puppets means a thousand stakes, so forgery costs more than honest participation.
